Subject: Data residency carveouts and temporary egress authorization (CardioTech / Redwood)

Hi Mateo / Kimberly —

Thanks for the product overview last week. We have a couple of final open items from our legal & procurement teams before we can sign the DPA:

1) Can Redwood commit to EU-only residency for "CardioTech Health" production workloads, except for a defined temporary egress window for disaster recovery or load balancing?
2) If a temporary cross-border hop occurs, what is the maximum duration and how will you notify our DPO? We need a binding SLA window (ideally <= 96 hours) plus telemetry.
3) We also need a current subprocessor roster and a process for swaps during renewals.

Attached is our DPA template with some suggested edits. Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept a conditional sovereignty clause that permits transient egress for up to 72 hours with prior notification + audit logs?

Thanks — I can get procurement on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Anna
Anna Chung
Head of Procurement, CardioTech Health
Attachments: CardioTech_DPA_v1.2.docx

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Data residency carveouts and temporary egress authorization (CardioTech / Redwood)

Hi Anna —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front:
- We can support EU-only placement for production models and data.
- We are open to a conditional sovereignty clause that allows transient cross-region processing for operational continuity, with firm controls.
- Standard transient window we propose: 72 hours for an operational failover, with written notification to the DPO within 4 hours of the event and a final post-incident report within 48 hours of restoration.

I'll loop in Marissa (legal) and Kimberly (Platform Security) to confirm the DPA redlines and the subprocessor swap process. For transparency, I'm attaching our current subprocessor roster and a draft redline of your DPA where we've noted required changes for KMS and transient-egress telemetry.

Proposed next step: 30-minute alignment call tomorrow (WED) 9am BST / 1am PDT — happy to adjust.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: subprocessor_roster_2027-05.xlsx; redline_DPA_mco_mta.docx

Subject: Re: Data residency carveouts and temporary egress authorization (CardioTech / Redwood)

Hi Anna —

Thanks for the DPA draft. I reviewed the conditional sovereignty language and added targeted redlines where we need clarifications or alternative phrasing. Key points to call out:

• Transient egress definition: We limited the allowable transient processing to strictly "stateless routing" and infrastructure-level caching required for failover (no persistent writes outside EU without explicit addendum).
• Maximum transient window: we can accept up to 72 hours for emergency failover but we require an explicit restart/renewal trigger if an event extends beyond 72 hours.
• Notification & audit: Redwood will provide DPO-level notification within 4 hours and a signed post-incident report including KSOs (kernel-level routing logs) and the token-level telemetry for affected flows within 48 hours.
• Subprocessor swaps: we can agree to a 30-day notice for non-critical swaps, 7-day notice for critical substitutions, and an emergency override process where we notify downstream customers within 24 hours and provide an escrowed justification.

I left in-track changes in the attached redline (see sections 3.2 and 9.1). We would like to get legal sign-off from your DPO on the telemetry scope (token-level telemetry is sensitive; we'll accept aggregated telemetry plus event-level evidence on request).

If helpful, Kimberly and I can join a short call with your legal team to walk through the redline. Proposed times: Thu 10am BST or Thu 2pm BST.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Legal (Contracts), Redwood Inference
Attachments: redline_DPA_mco_mta.docx

From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@cardiotech.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: anna.chung@cardiotech.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency carveouts and temporary egress authorization (CardioTech / Redwood)

Marissa / Mateo —

Thanks for the rapid responses and the redlines. A few clarifying points from the DPO side before we lock in the language:

1) Telemetry minimums: We need an inventory of the exact telemetry fields Redwood will provide in the 48-hour post-incident report (timestamped routing events, source/destination region, affected tenant IDs, and a redacted token count). Aggregated metrics are fine for rolling reports, but the post-incident must include event-level items listed above.
2) Escrow justification: For emergency swaps, please confirm the escrow mechanism (signed statement, timestamped logs, and an attestation by your Security Officer).
3) Contractual remedy: If transient egress occurs without the notification window (4 hours), we need a one-time remediation credit and an SLA uplift for monitoring until the next billing cycle.

If Redwood can provide a short appendix that enumerates the telemetry fields and the escrow attestation template, I can get procurement to proceed. We can aim to finalize the DPA after reviewing the appendix and the redline call.

Regards,
Rajiv Patel
Data Protection Officer, CardioTech Health
